title: Bug: Sandbox container not stopped after terminal run despite stop_on_terminal=true
description:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (2026-08-21, clean repro):

GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/files restarts the stopped sandbox container of a TERMINAL run and never stops it again.

Mechanism:
- run_files.rs:1201 reconnect_run_sandbox() calls sandbox.activate() unconditionally (line 1220)
- DockerSandbox::activate() -> begin_start() -> docker start on the stopped container
- Nothing ever stops it afterwards (auto_stop=null, worker already exited) -> leaked running container per visited finished run

Repro (3 steps, verified):
1. fabro run context-demo --environment default -> run succeeds, container Exited (stop_on_terminal works)
2. GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/files?scope=committed (dev-token) -> HTTP 200, container state flips to "Up"
3. Server log: "Sandbox start completed" AFTER the run's "Sandbox stop completed"

Also affected (same pattern): handler/sandbox.rs:884 (GET /runs/{id}/sandbox/files), sessions.rs:734. Terminal WS (handler/sandbox.rs:930) activates intentionally.

Historical evidence: containers 01M0GJVW659C / 01M0GG56PQYP were stopped correctly yesterday (FinishedAt, ExitCode 0) and were silently restarted today 08:04/08:05 by web-UI page visits (2 parallel sandbox starts each, matching /files + /sandbox/files in flight).

Fix options (decision needed):
A) Serve terminal-run files from git checkpoint/final_patch instead of activating the sandbox (final_patch fallback already exists; committed scope could come from checkpoint branch store)
B) Ref-counted activation: stop container again after serving when run is terminal AND lifecycle.stop_on_terminal
C) Gate: refuse to activate sandboxes of terminal runs -> degraded response

Note: with container deleted, /files degrades gracefully to source=final_patch (HTTP 200), proving option A/C are viable.

title: Workflow: per-node tool policy attribute (allow/deny tools per agent stage)
description:
## Problem

Workflow agent stages run with NO tool_access_policy: create_session_for (fabro-workflow/src/handler/llm/api.rs ~1096) sets permission_level=Full with the comment 'Override per-stage if a future workflow attribute narrows the scope' — that attribute does not exist. Every agent node gets the entire tool registry (shell, write_file, edit_file, spawn_agent, MCP). The only existing restriction is binary: prompt nodes (shape=tab) get NO tools at all.

## DECIDED DESIGN (2026-08-27 grilling; amends ADR-0009 — see its 2026-08-27 section)

Allow-only, ONE attribute, no presets, no deny, no run-level policy:

- tools='read_file,grep,glob' — allow-list of CANONICAL tool names; unset = default open (full registry). Everything not named is denied (incl. MCP tools, spawn_agent, fabro_run_*). Profile vocabularies (Kimi Read/Grep/Glob) resolved via canonical_tool_name().
- Presets DROPPED (ADR-0009 amendment): blackbox risk; explicit lists self-document and never leak new catalog tools. Presets may return later if lists grow unwieldy.
- Question tools (request_user_input, AskUserQuestion) exempt BOTH ways (is_question_tool predicate): HITL is a workflow contract, like engine-stamped keys in 900e.
- spawn_agent only when explicitly named; child sessions (SessionFactory) inherit the same allow-list.
- permission_level UNTOUCHED (stays Full): upstream's interactive CLI approval axis (is_auto_approved, cli.rs:153), wire-contracted in OpenAPI. No derivation, no removal. Policy narrowing shows in the agent_tools projection (agent.tools.available event + StageProjection) which the web UI already renders (stage-insights-sidebar). Update the api.rs comment accordingly.
- Per-node fabro_tools='fabro_run_get,fabro_run_logs' — opt-in list from the static fabro_tool catalog; OVERRIDES the run-wide agent.fabro_tools flag; unset keeps run default (false). Uses existing register_named_fabro_run_tools. Default-denied opt-in family — opposite posture of the default-open native registry.

## Validation (fabro-validate; single-line format! diagnostics per mx-f60828)

- Warn on unknown names in tools/fabro_tools (native + fabro_run catalogs are statically known; mcp__-prefixed names exempt — they depend on run config).
- Warn on tools/fabro_tools set on non-agent nodes (prompt nodes: useless there).

## Implementation shape

- fabro-agent: productize NamedToolAccessPolicy (test-only today) into production code; Allowed/Denied only (workflow sessions have no approval path; RequiresApproval would silently equal Denied).
- fabro-types/graph.rs: typed accessors tools() + fabro_tools() beside context_allow_keys (split_key_list precedent), doc comments citing seed + ADR-0009.
- fabro-workflow create_session_for: build the policy from the node attribute, thread it into SessionOptions.tool_access_policy and the child factory.
- Docs in the same change (ADR-0008): docs/public/execution + docs_options_reference; ADR-0009 amendment already landed.

## Verification plan

Unit tests: parsing (split/trim), classification (canonical names incl. Kimi vocabulary), effective_tools filtering + execution denial, question-tool exemption, child inheritance; e2e scenario like 900e (denied tool neither exposed nor executable; projection shows effective list); validate rule tests. fmt + clippy -D warnings; types+agent+validate+workflow suites green.

## Use cases (lab)

Planner restricted to read tools (prompt rule only today — the model CAN shell out); reviewer read-only without losing tool-driven stages; implementer without spawn_agent/MCP; implementer with scoped fabro_run_get instead of blind .fabro/ probing (run 01M0NJ3QZ1FK53X9DK3BBAN2ED).

## SESSION STATE 2026-08-28 (session ended BEFORE implementation)

DONE: design decided in grill-with-docs (all forks settled); ADR-0009 amendment landed (commit 0c54f3cc4); mulch decisions recorded; upstream drift analysis delivered.

Drift analysis summary: changes are additive on upstream-owned surfaces; the api.rs 'Override per-stage' comment is upstream's own invitation (upstream/main api.rs:1086-1089); permission_level untouched = zero wire drift; biggest drift driver is TIME + the un-offered envelope family (graph.rs already 204 diff lines from 900e), NOT this design. Offer order when upstream reacts to our open PRs: 900e then 47b5. Keep upstream-plausible shapes (NamedToolAccessPolicy name, accessor style, rule-file-per-rule).

NEXT (Phase 2 Build): load rust-style-guide pages enums-vs-traits-vs-generics-vs-trait-objects, newtype-pattern-and-semantic-wrappers, validation-and-invariants, error-taxonomy-and-layer-boundaries, struct-design-and-encapsulation, testing-and-doctests + workflows/code-review-refactor.md for Phase 3; then implement per 'Implementation shape' above; verify per 'Verification plan'. Working tree is clean; branch is denkhaus; no other in-progress local work (6a78/af22 wait on upstream PRs #786/#784, both still OPEN 2026-08-28).

---

## CLOSED 2026-08-31 (commit c867a1a8c)

Delivered per the decided design, all ten decided points implemented
(allow-only canonical list, question-tool exemption both ways, child
inheritance, permission_level untouched, fabro_tools override, validate
rules with live cross-checks, docs in the same change). Wire-level
proof via httpmock + real AgentApiBackend: scoped node sends exactly
read_file+grep, projection shows the allow-list plus the exempt
question tool, default-open node keeps the full registry.

Verification: nextest 4970/4970 (6 packages), clippy -D warnings clean,
fmt clean, web 825/825 + typecheck.

Process note: the first e2e draft (twin + CodergenBackend) was a false
positive — that seam bypasses agent sessions entirely, and
--profile e2e silently skips twin-only tests (NEXTEST_PROFILE=e2e =>
Strict). Both review sub-agents caught it (their replies were lost but
transcripts show the finding; reproduced independently). The shipped
httpmock test runs in the default profile and asserts on the WIRE
request body, which the twin draft never touched.

- Node attrs fs_hide/fs_write (flat snake_case) in fabro-types graph.rs accessors.
- FsScope + ScopedSandbox decorator in fabro-sandbox/src/fs_scope.rs: nonexistent semantics (reads fail, file_exists=false, grep/glob/list_dir/walk_files filtered, writes denied), dir/** also hides the dir entry (added during build: pure-glob semantics leaked the directory), write allowlist with empty=read-only, outside-workspace reads pass through / writes denied when fs_write set, exec delegates (documented escape hatch). title: Workflow: per-node context_updates allowlist + append-only arrays
description:
## IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-27, denkhaus dc5959a80) — first of the ADR-0009 family

- fabro-types: Node::context_allow_keys (Option<Vec<&str>>, unset = default-open) + Node::context_append_keys, shared split_key_list parsing (trimmed, empty entries dropped); RunNoticeCode::ContextUpdateDropped
- fabro-workflow: context::enforce_stage_envelope + lifecycle/envelope.rs (EnvelopeLifecycle, runs FIRST in after_node — events, hooks, checkpoint, state.record all see admitted updates only). Drops: scoped run.notice (Warn, code context_update_dropped, node in envelope, sorted keys in message). Append merge: stages emit the delta; engine merges onto the accumulated absolute array (checkpoint replay + edge conditions stay last-writer-wins); legacy scalar/object wraps as first entry; engine-stamped keys keep replace semantics; response.* exemption scoped to the node's OWN key (cross-node response spoofing stays droppable — review hardening from the code-review round)
- fabro-validate: context_append_keys_within_allow warns when an append key sits outside a set allowlist
- docs: 'Ownership and accumulation' section in docs/public/execution/context.mdx (semantics, engine-key list, parallel-branch limitation)
- verification: 16 dedicated tests incl. end-to-end scenario stage_envelope_drops_and_accumulates_end_to_end (real executor: drop + notice + append merge); fmt/clippy -D warnings clean; types+validate+workflow+server suites green

## v1 DESIGN DECISIONS (from the review round, documented)

- Prompt-mention validate warning NOT built (spec narrowing): scanning prompt text for key names is fragile prose-matching; the engine drop+notice is the authoritative, always-correct signal. Revisit only if lab runs show agents repeatedly attempting forbidden writes without noticing the notice.
- Engine-stamped key exemption: ADR-0009 drift-protection posture, not adversarial containment. Agent re-declaration of engine keys (last_stage/outcome/...) is neutralized because handlers stamp them into the same map after model parsing.
- Parallel branch limitation documented: branch updates land in engine-stamped parallel.results, so the envelope binds sequential nodes and the parallel node, not branch targets.

Follow-ups filed: fabro-8822 (pre-existing clap parse test failures found during gating). Next family member per build order: fabro-47b5 (per-node tool policy).

title: Workflow: preamble value demotion (8KB) makes tool-less reviewers blind; per-node inline budget needed
description:
## IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-26, denkhaus baf84a2bd): preamble_inline_max_kb — option 1 of the proposal

A prompt node raises its per-value inline ceiling so evidence-sized values
stay inline (the node can never open the demotion marker's file reference).
- fabro-types: Graph::preamble_inline_max_kb + Node override (<1 ignored);
  shared defaults DEFAULT_PREAMBLE_INLINE_MAX_KB=8 / DEFAULT_PREAMBLE_BUDGET_KB=12
- artifact.rs: demote_large_values_for_prompt takes inline_max; aggregate
  budget still bounds the sum
- fidelity.rs: resolution node > graph > 8KB default
- validate: warning preamble_inline_max_within_budget (ceiling above budget
  re-demotes what it kept inline)
- docs: context.mdx 'Raising the per-value ceiling' (incl. >=100KB blob-offload
  interplay: those never render inline regardless)
- tests: attr parse, fidelity node-override + control demotes, graph ceiling,
  4 lint cases; 2150/2150 types+validate+workflow, 2580/2580
  sandbox+server+api+cli, CLI validate 34/34; deployed via just up (smoke 7/7)

Remaining: lab adoption — set preamble_inline_max_kb=16 on the develop
reviewer node on meta/denkhaus-lab at the next lab sync. inline_refs
(option 2) deliberately not built; revisit only if inline-max proves
insufficient in the loop.

## STATUS UPDATE (2026-08-23): aggregate half absorbed by fabro-a85b

a85b's aggregate demote pass (16KB sum over all preamble values,
largest-first, 1KB floor) is the generalized fix: many sub-8KB values
now demote too. The SPECIFIC tool-less-reviewer blind spot (a single
8.3KB evidence value demoted to a 300-char preview a prompt node can
never open) is NOT solved by the budget — it needs either the evidence
carve-out (a85b design decision 2) or read-tools via fabro-47b5.
Keep THIS seed open for that reviewer-fidelity question; re-scope
after a85b lands and the lab loop is re-measured.

## Bug

artifact.rs demotes any context/preamble value over
PROMPT_INLINE_VALUE_MAX (8KB) to a 300-char preview plus a blob/file
reference. Downstream agents are expected to READ the referenced file —
but a prompt node (shape=tab) has NO tools and can never open it.
Evidence-style command output above 8KB is therefore structurally
invisible to the one node designed to judge it.

## Observed failure

Run 01M0NGQXB67674XQ5YCR1MB4BN: evidence output reached 8.3KB; the
reviewer (prompt node, fidelity=summary:high) received a 4-line preview
and a blob path, rejected twice with 'identical defect', and the loop
could not converge (implementer is barred from fixing the platform-side
evidence script; cancellation required). Painpoint delivered to the
platform mailbox (meta/denkhaus-lab painpoints.jsonl).

## Proposal

One or both:
1. Per-node or graph attribute raising the inline budget for designated
   nodes (e.g. inline_max='16k'), letting workflow authors pay tokens
   for full-fidelity review.
2. A preamble directive that inlines the materialized blob content for
   designated refs (e.g. inline_refs='command.output') regardless of
   size — engine-controlled, no new tool access.

## Acceptance

- attribute parsed + validated (bounds, interplay with artifact
  offloading documented)
- demotion respects it; preamble shows full value
- docs: context.md 'Artifact offloading' gains the attribute and the
  tool-less-reviewer caveat
Created:  2026-08-22T20:20:28.283Z
Updated:  2026-08-26T11:25:19.687Z
closeReason: Implemented and verified (baf84a2bd): preamble_inline_max_kb graph+node attribute, validate warning preamble_inline_max_within_budget, docs, full test suites green, deployed. Lab adoption (reviewer node, meta/denkhaus-lab) is the follow-up at next lab sync; inline_refs option not needed for v1.

description:
## Problem

Run lifecycle control is API-only. The CLI covers lifecycle narrowly and
implicitly:

- CANCEL exists only as Ctrl+C on an ATTACHED run (kill_on_detach=true is
  hardcoded in command.rs when run attaches; attach.rs handle_detach_signal
  calls client.cancel_run). For a run started with --detach (the natural
  pattern for long/autonomous runs), a run started by someone else, or an
  automation-triggered run, there is NO CLI way to cancel — users fall
  back to curl POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/cancel with a bearer token from
  ~/.fabro/auth.json (which is what happened in the denkhaus lab, twice).
- INTERRUPT (/interrupt: forward to worker, abort in-flight LLM), PAUSE,
  RETRY have server routes but no CLI commands at all.
- rm --force deletes active runs (destructive) — not a substitute for a
  graceful cancel.

## Proposal

Add run-control commands with run-ID prefix resolution (like attach):

  fabro cancel  <RUN> [--wait]   # graceful cancel, --wait polls to terminal
  fabro interrupt <RUN>          # API /interrupt (abort in-flight stage)
  fabro pause <RUN> / unpause    # API /pause
  fabro retry <RUN>              # API /retry

cancel maps to the existing client.cancel_run used by the attach path —
same semantics as Ctrl+C, just addressable after the fact.

Suggested alias: a --kill flag on  is NOT needed; the
attach-Ctrl+C path already covers it.

## Acceptance

- fabro cancel works for any non-terminal run the user can see, with
  prefix resolution and clear error for terminal runs
- --wait blocks until terminal state (bounded)
- docs: CLI reference gains the run-control section
- tests mirror handle_detach_signal_with_kill_on_detach_* semantics

title: Agent harness: parallel edit_file calls to the same file silently clobber each other
description:
## Bug

From run 01M0NJZGX7BMJAJC3CZJZ0RNT0 review (mulch mx-eba2dd): the
implementer issued parallel edit_file calls targeting ONE file; they
silently clobbered each other — 'lost a strconv import and two run()
call-site updates; caught later by go vet'. Parallel tool execution
(sessions support it) has no same-target write serialization or conflict
detection.

## Why it matters

A silent lost edit is worse than a failed one: the model believes its
edit landed; nothing errors; only a downstream gate or review catches
the drift — if it does.

## Proposal (any or all)

1. Serialize write-tools per file path (mutex keyed on target path)
2. Detect conflicting parallel writes and fail the second with a clear
   'concurrent edit to <path>' error the model can retry sequentially
3. At minimum: apply order-deterministically (by call order, not
   completion race) and log a warning event

## Acceptance

- test: two parallel edit_file calls to one file apply BOTH edits (or
  the second errors visibly), never silently drop
- warning event emitted on same-file parallel writes
- docs: tools.md parallel-execution section states the guarantee

title: Run status: 'succeeded' when the goal is not achieved (seed still open) — boundary state needed
description:
## Problem

Run 01M0NJZGX7BMJAJC3CZJZ0RNT0: status succeeded(completed) while seed
fabro-0879 is still in_progress and the goal ('until no open seed
remains') is not met. The graph honestly routes reviewer-failure to
exit with the seed open, but the top-level status misleads automation
and humans alike ('succeeded' implies done).

## Proposal

- A distinct terminal status for 'run ended at a boundary': e.g.
  succeeded_boundary / incomplete (or a conclusion marker
  'N seeds awaiting review')
- The run conclusion should surface the natural next action
  ('re-run to resume review') instead of leaving it inferred

## Acceptance

- run conclusion carries goal-vs-boundary distinction
- API/UI show it; CLI summary prints 'boundary: N seed(s) still open'
- docs: outcomes.md or run-lifecycle doc names the state

title: Preamble: strip trailing routing JSON from rendered responses; dedupe context re-reads
description:
## Problem

Run 01M0NJZGX7BMJAJC3CZJZ0RNT0 billed 828k tokens (~$0.40), largely
re-reading duplicated context: the seed brief appears 3-4x per
downstream prompt (planner's full response INCLUDING its trailing
routing JSON, the current_seed_brief context value, and the
implementer's echo in implementation_summary). The routing JSON
duplicates context_updates verbatim.

## Proposal

1. When rendering a stage response into later preambles, strip the
   trailing routing directive (it is data for the engine, not context
   for peers — the parsed context_updates already carry it)
2. Render each context value once (brief in the context table; do not
   also embed it in the response echo)
3. Optional: instruct/allow agents to keep responses terse (done in the
   lab prompts as a stopgap)

## Acceptance

- preamble contains exactly one copy of each context key
- routing JSON absent from rendered peer context
- token accounting on a comparable run drops measurably

title: Skill discovery loads ~36 irrelevant skills into every agent stage (~1.5k tokens)
description:
## Problem

Every agent session in the lab loads ~36 skill descriptions
(scaffold-exercises, shoehorn migration, ...) — ~1.5k tokens per stage,
almost entirely irrelevant to the loop roles. Skills are a repo-wide
concept but stages have narrow needs.

## Proposal

- per-node skill scoping (skills='seeds,mulch' or skills.none), or
- lazy loading (descriptions only on demand — the agent asks for a
  catalog tool), or
- skill groups in .fabro/skills config mapped to node labels

## Acceptance

- a node can run with zero or scoped skill descriptions
- per-stage prompt size drops accordingly
- docs: skills.md gains the scoping section

## Upstream watch (2026-08-26)

Upstream PR #751 (open, unreviewed since 2026-08-17, fork PR, closes #746)
adds run-level `[run.agent] skill_dirs` — EXTRA discovery dirs, additive
after conventions, plumbed RunAgentSettings -> run spec -> LlmSpec ->
SessionOptions.extra_skill_dirs. Complementary only: it widens discovery
for ALL stages and does not scope per node, so it does not address this
seed. If it lands, per-node scoping should reuse that plumbing
(LlmSpec/SessionOptions) and add a node-level allow/deny layer —
the model_stylesheet per-node pattern is the template for node-level
config precedence.

## Family naming (2026-08-26, ADR-0009)

This seed joins the stage-envelope family naming: flat snake_case
attribute, e.g. skills_allow='...' / skills_none. Default stays open;
per-node explicit restriction only.

title: Sandbox: docker provider should auto-build from image.dockerfile (like daytona) with content-hash caching
description:
## Problem

DockerfileSource (image.dockerfile, inline or path) is consumed ONLY by
the daytona provider (snapshot build + dockerfile_sha256 cache key).
The docker provider accepts just image.docker = 'name:tag' — a finished
image. Repos that run docker sandboxes must bake runner images outside
fabro (manual docker build or external CI), or pay per-run toolchain
setup: in the denkhaus lab, mise install costs ~24.5s of every ~32s run
setup (run 01M0NJZGX7BMJAJC3CZJZ0RNT0, events seq 13-14).

## Proposal

docker provider: when image.dockerfile is set (instead of image.docker),
build the image on first use, tag it from the dockerfile content hash
(e.g. fabro-runner-<sha12>), and reuse it while the hash matches — the
same caching discipline daytona applies to snapshots. Runner-image-as-
config then travels with the repo: .fabro/Dockerfile.* + [run.environment]
image.dockerfile path.

## Acceptance

- image.dockerfile works for provider=docker (inline and path forms)
- image is built once per content hash; unchanged dockerfile = no rebuild
- build failures surface as clear preflight/sandbox errors
- docs: environments.mdx docker section documents the field + caching
- a lab-validated example (mise runner) linked in the ticket

title: Preamble delivery: aggregate demote budget + per-node stage scoping (upstream vocabulary)
description:
## VOCABULARY CORRECTION (2026-08-23): upstream terms only

This seed previously invented 'Persistor'/'handle'/'outcomes/ files'.
Code research showed upstream already names every piece:

- OFFLOAD: persist a value into the content-addressed blob store
  (>100KB context values become blob://sha256/... refs, artifact.rs)
- DEMOTE: replace an inline preamble value with a preview+path marker
  (>8KB per value, PROMPT_INLINE_VALUE_MAX, marker = PromptLargeValue)
- BLOB REF / ARTIFACT POINTER: the references (blob://..., file://...)
- OUTCOME: upstream type (fabro-types/outcome.rs); responses are
  already captured to stages/{rank:03}-{node_id}@{visit}/response.md +
  status.json on the METADATA BRANCH (not materialized in the worktree)
- MATERIALIZE: placing a file into the sandbox worktree (demote does
  this for demoted values)

'Persistor', 'handle', 'handle delivery', 'outcomes/ dir' are retired.

## DESIGN CHANGE (grilled, R1+): NO interface, no strategy trait

The original vision (deterministic persistor writing .fabro/outcomes/)
is replaced by a minimal fix at the EXISTING seam:

Root cause (verified in code): demote_large_values_for_prompt
(lifecycle/fidelity.rs:204, called once before build_preamble) checks
values INDIVIDUALLY against 8KB. Nine ~3KB responses sum to 25.6k with
no trigger. Also summary:high renders sub-8KB LLM responses fully as
blockquotes (preamble.rs:280) — no line cap.

Fix 1 — AGGREGATE BUDGET PASS: after the per-value pass, sum serialized
sizes of all non-hidden values + outcome updates; if over
PREAMBLE_VALUE_BUDGET (16KB default), demote largest-first until under
budget; values <1KB are never demoted by this pass (contract keys,
enums stay inline for free — no keep-inline list needed). Renderer
already renders the demote marker at all 6 sites incl. response
blockquotes; demote materializes full values as sandbox files (pull
access exists). Zero renderer changes.

Fix 2 — PER-NODE STAGE SCOPING (deny-list): attribute
preamble_stages_ignore = "planner,refiner" on a node omits those
stages' history sections from ITS preamble (thematic selection,
e47c-family). Filter applies render-only in fidelity.rs before
build_preamble; context store untouched (routing, response.* keys,
other consumers unaffected). stage_rendered_keys dedup means ignored
stages' context_updates (e.g. seed brief) still render in the Context
section — exactly what a reviewer needs.

Validation: new lint preamble_stages_ignore_targets_exist in
fabro-validate, Severity::Warning (retry_target_exists precedent:
nonexistent node refs warn, run proceeds; runtime filter matches by
node id, a no-op for missing entries).

Allow-list (preamble_stages=...) deliberately NOT in v1: inverts the
default (opt-in vs today's pass-through); documented follow-up.

## FORK-FIRST (agreed)

Do not gate dev pace on maintainer decisions. Develop on
feat/preamble-stage-scoping (denkhaus base), lab verifies, PR upstream
as an offer. Adopt maintainer's approach only if strictly better.

## Acceptance (updated)

- aggregate pass keeps preamble constant-size across >=3 loop cycles
  (lab assertion, many sub-8KB values reproducer)
- preamble_stages_ignore omits named stages' sections; warning (not
  error) on nonexistent entries; fabro validate covers it
- docs: context.mdx + preamble section use upstream vocabulary
- stages/ materialization split out (see new seed) — no longer blocking

## Supersedes/absorbs

- absorbs: aggregate-budget half of fabro-9467
- realizes deny-list half of fabro-e47c
- companions: fabro-e804 (context_read resolves blob refs/materialized
  files), fabro-900e, fabro-47b5 unchanged

## IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (in progress, branch feat/preamble-stage-scoping)

Commit 1 — preamble_stages_ignore:
1. Node attribute parse: follow the fidelity/retry_target accessor
   pattern in fabro-graphviz Node (comma-separated list, trim, dedupe;
   empty entries dropped)
2. Filter in lifecycle/fidelity.rs BEFORE build_preamble: drop ignored
   node ids from completed_nodes (and their outcomes from the map
   passed to the renderer) — render-only, resolved copies only
3. Lint rule fabro-validate/rules/preamble_stages_ignore_targets_exist
   (Severity::Warning, retry_target_exists shape) + tests
4. Docs: context.mdx preamble/fidelity section

Commit 2 — aggregate budget pass:
5. artifact.rs: PREAMBLE_VALUE_BUDGET (16KB) + PREAMBLE_DEMOTE_FLOOR
   (1KB); after per-value pass in demote_large_values_for_prompt,
   sort candidates by serialized size desc, demote until sum <= budget
   (reuse demote_value_for_prompt; skip already-demoted markers)
6. Tests: (a) many ~3KB values -> aggregate demotes, preamble const;
   (b) small contract keys stay inline; (c) single 20KB value still
   demoted per-value (unchanged); (d) exactly-at-budget boundary
7. Docs: outputs.mdx demote section gains the aggregate budget

Then: lab loop verify (>=3 cycles, preamble size stable), PR upstream
as offer (fork-first posture per ADR-0007).

title: Document + decide: preamble_stages_ignore does not apply per parallel-branch target
description:
## Finding (code-verified, 2026-08-23)

preamble_stages_ignore on a PARALLEL-BRANCH TARGET node is silently
ignored. Verified against the fan-out path:

- Branch preambles are PRE-RENDERED by build_parallel_branch_preambles
  in lifecycle/fidelity.rs, from the PARENT parallel node's before_node
  pass, using the parent's scoping (comment in code: 'Branch preambles
  inherit the parent node's stage scoping').
- Branch target nodes never run before_node themselves (known branch
  path: handler/parallel.rs execute_single_attempt, no lifecycle), so a
  preamble_stages_ignore attribute set on the target has no execution
  point where it could apply.
- The attribute WORKS on: the parent parallel node (applies to ALL
  branch preambles), fan-in nodes with prompts (standard prompt path),
  and all sequential nodes.

## Risk

A workflow author sets scoping on a branch target expecting per-branch
filtering; it silently does nothing. The branch preamble renders all
stage history the parent did not filter. No warning, no validation
error.

## Required work

1. DOCS: context.mdx 'Stage scoping (deny-list)' section gains an
   explicit limitation note: attribute placement on parallel branch
   targets is ignored; set it on the parent parallel node to scope all
   branch preambles.
2. VALIDATION: new fabro-validate rule (warning, inert-attribute
   family like parallel_branch_inert_attribute.rs — PRECEDENT EXISTS):
   'preamble_stages_ignore on parallel branch target X is inert; move
   it to the parent parallel node'. That rule file already flags inert
   fidelity on branch targets — extend the family.
3. DECISION (upstream-facing): either accept the limitation as the
   documented contract (parent-scoped inheritance) or implement
   per-branch scoping by honoring the target's attribute inside
   build_parallel_branch_preambles (needs the target node's own
   preamble_stages_ignore read at pre-render time — data is available:
   target_node is resolved there). Fork-first: docs+lint now on our
   branch; upstream PR offer later.

## Evidence

- lifecycle/fidelity.rs: build_parallel_branch_preambles receives
  completed_nodes/node_outcomes from the PARENT's scoped copies only
- handler/parallel.rs: branch path skips lifecycle before_node
- existing inert-attribute precedent:
  fabro-validate/src/rules/parallel_branch_inert_attribute.rs

title: PR publish robustness: dedicated model + reasoning_effort for PR content; deterministic fallback on LLM failure
description:
## Failure (run 01M0QTNF6GWHGPKHSQ2Y2PB8CQ)

Everything green (loop, gate, review approved, seed closed, run branch
pushed) — then the run FAILED with publish_failed: the PR title/body
generator (single structured LLM call, run model glm-5.3) returned no
JSON ('expected value at line 1 column 1'). glm-5.3 without explicitly
disabled reasoning tends to non-JSON output for structured requests;
the PR call sets NO reasoning_effort (GenerateParams field exists,
wired nowhere in pull_request.rs) — provider default applies.

## Root causes (both code-verified)

1. NO PR-specific model config: build_pr_content uses the run model;
   [run.pull_request] has enabled/draft/auto_merge but no model.
2. reasoning_effort not configurable for the publish step (RunModelControls
   has it for NODES; the PR call bypasses node controls).
3. No fallback on LLM HARD failure: fallback_pr_title(goal) exists but
   only triggers on EMPTY generated title — a failed generate_object
   propagates via ? and kills the run (publish_failed), despite a
   perfect deterministic title (seed title / goal) being available.

## Fix (upstream-PR candidate after the preamble package)

1. [run.pull_request] model = 'zai/glm-4.7-flash' (falls back to run
   model) — decouples cheap titling from the working model
2. [run.pull_request] reasoning_effort passthrough to
   GenerateParams.reasoning_effort (e.g. 'off' for glm-4.7-flash)
3. generate_object error -> warn! + fallback_pr_title(goal) + skeleton
   body; hard failure only when even the fallback cannot form
4. Tests: LLM hard-fail -> run still publishes with fallback title;
   configured model+effort reach the adapter

## Evidence

- log: 'Pull request creation failed error=LLM generation failed: No
  object generated: Failed to parse response as JSON'
- pipeline/pull_request.rs:401 (GenerateParams::new without reasoning),
  :408-411 (map_err + ? propagation), :415-419 (fallback only for empty)
- run branch ee9ca7591 was merged manually (8d26 delivered)

title: Ask Fabro: sessions.rs activate() has no lifecycle guard — terminal runs can leak sandboxes
description:
Split from fabro-52f2 (closed 2026-08-24): the inspection-endpoint leak was fixed by 4b77f11c7 (InspectionSandbox guard, SandboxActivation::Started/AlreadyActive). One activate() site stayed outside that fix.

## Bug
lib/apps/fabro-server/src/server/handler/sessions.rs:734 (Ask Fabro session build) calls bare sandbox.activate() with no InspectionSandbox guard and no run-status check. Opening an Ask Fabro session on a TERMINAL run starts the stopped sandbox and nothing ever stops it again — same leak class as the fixed inspection endpoints.

Why the guard does not simply apply: Ask Fabro is a long-lived chat session that NEEDS the sandbox while it lives. This is a different lifecycle concept from read-only inspection (short request, stop on exit):

- read-only inspection: request-scoped, guard restores stopped state on exit
- session-held sandbox: the session OWNS the liveness; sandbox stops when the session ends/expires

## Proposal (decision part of this seed)
Design a session-held-sandbox lifecycle: track that the session activated the sandbox, stop it when the session ends or expires. Consider the degraded alternative for terminal runs (agent runs, sandbox tools answer with a clear error) as the fallback if session-scoped liveness proves too heavy.

## Acceptance
- Ask Fabro session on a terminal run does not leak a running container after session end/expiry
- test covering the terminal-run session path
- vocabulary: keep 'read-only inspection' vs 'session-held sandbox' distinct in code comments

---

## Implementation design (2026-08-31, before code)

Revised by 0c32 reality: the revisor's fabro_ask targets terminal runs
daily — this is the hot path, not an edge.

Chosen: TURN-SCOPED liveness for terminal runs (variant A2 of the
proposal). The projected runtime_context carries the full conversation
(Vec<SessionMessage>), so rebuilding the Session per turn is
stateless-correct; the cached-session optimization exists only for
cost. For a TERMINAL run the turn builds the session (activating the
sandbox), runs the turn, then EVICTS the session slot and STOPS the
sandbox when the activation started it — mirroring
inspection_should_stop exactly.

Three sandbox lifecycles, distinct in comments (acceptance vocabulary):
- read-only inspection: request-scoped guard, restores stopped state
- active-run Ask-Fabro session: cached; the run lifecycle owns liveness
- terminal-run Ask-Fabro session: turn-scoped; the turn owns liveness

Shape: build_agent_session returns (Session, Option<Arc<dyn Sandbox>>)
— Some means this build STARTED the sandbox of a terminal run and the
caller must stop it after the turn's terminal event. submit_turn holds
the guard outside the session-slot borrow, stops best-effort (warn!)
after all three turn outcomes, evicts the slot via the existing
clear_session.

fabro_agent::Sandbox IS fabro_sandbox::Sandbox (re-export) — stop() is
reachable on the Arc handed to the Session; clone before moving in.

Tests: unit — decision fn (terminal x Started => owned; non-terminal
never; AlreadyActive never). Server — terminal run with unreachable
sandbox record fails the turn cleanly (proves the terminal build path).
Full wire proof (turn on terminal run stops the container) folds into
fabro-3b6d, which already demands the full ask-chain e2e rig.

---

## CLOSED 2026-08-31 (commit edbc84cfd)

Turn-scoped liveness implemented per the design section. Guard
(Option<TurnScopedSandbox>) only when activation==Started AND run
terminal; evict+stop after every turn outcome; inline stop on the
from_record build-error path (review F2). Hermetic server test proves
the terminal-run build path + two successful analyst turns; the
eviction/stop wire proof (fake Started provider or Docker/Daytona rig)
rides on fabro-3b6d, which now points at this test's scaffolding
(jwt_auth_state_with_openai_base_url + Responses-SSE httpmock +
ServerDaemon fixture). Verification: 878/878 fabro-server, clippy
clean, fmt clean, web 825/825.

title: engine: deterministic per-seed cycle counter as context key
description:
## Failure mode

The develop workflow's 3-strikes cycle guard relies on the planner LLM
counting review/gate cycles from preamble history (run 01M0T9B7T6
review, recommendation 1b). A hallucinated count blocks a seed too
early or lets it loop past budget. The engine already tracks
node_visits deterministically; the planner just cannot see it per seed.

## Fix

Deterministic cycle counts injected as a context key, anchored on the
context key that carries seed identity:

- graph attribute (optional), e.g. cycle_counter_reset_key =
  "current_seed_id" — the context key whose VALUE change marks a new
  seed cycle context (engine stays seed-agnostic; the workflow names
  its own key).
- On each stage completion, if the completed node's context_updates
  contain the reset key with a value DIFFERENT from the tracked one,
  snapshot the per-node visit counts as the new baseline.
- Inject internal.seed_cycles = { node -> visits_since_baseline } so
  agents read deterministic counts (reviewer visits since this seed
  was claimed, tester bounces since, ...).
- The develop planner prompt (meta, follow-up) then replaces LLM
  counting with: 'blocked when internal.seed_cycles.reviewer >= 3'.

## Acceptance

- attribute unset -> behavior identical to today (no key injected)
- seed claimed mid-run -> counter starts at 0 for all nodes
- reviewer/tester revisits increment only the matching node counts
- new seed claim resets the baseline
- context key visible in stage preambles; unit tests cover baseline
  reset, increments, and the unset-attribute no-op

## Evidence

- ExecutionState.node_visits exists (fabro-core state.rs); Context has
  interior mutability (fidelity lifecycle writes CURRENT_PREAMBLE)

The seed brief appeared FOUR times per checkpoint: as
current_seed_brief, inside response.planner prose, again inside
response.planner's embedded JSON, plus checkpoint context copies. The
12 KB preamble budget blob-ref'd a 1.5 KB brief + 2.0 KB
implementation_summary — budget consumed by COPIES, not information.
And all soft exits (Capture failed, Blocked, Planner/Reviewer failed,
Tracker empty) route to ONE exit node, so run.completed/run.failed

and infrastructure failure.

## Fix

1. response.* dedup: when a stage's context_updates carry the same
   data the response text embeds (the JSON contract), stop persisting
   the full response text — or persist the parsed JSON payload only.
   At minimum: exclude context_updates keys that already exist as
   top-level keys from the response echo.
2. Distinct terminal nodes (or exit attributes): success /
   deadlock-for-human (Blocked) / infrastructure failure (capture,
   planner, reviewer) / natural completion (Tracker empty) so
   notification routes and the UI can distinguish them. Exit
   attributes are the smaller change if node identity must stay.
3. Tests: checkpoint context contains each fact exactly once (within a
   tolerance for goal/graph keys); terminal classification maps each
   exit path.

- existing workflows unchanged in behavior

Verification blocked re-capture: prompt-enforced only, so the loop is

closeReason: Same root cause as fabro-890b: stale server binary 0.335.0-nightly.1 pre-dated the dedicated PR model (a1e27c9bf), so glm-4.7 never fired at publish — glm-5.3 produced non-JSON and fell back (PR #2, runs 01M0TXPX/01M0X36). title: dev: spa_refresh mirror can leave the embedded assets dir empty (race/crash window)
description:
## Failure (evidence 2026-08-25, timeline)

Two overlapping 'just up' runs raced around 12:09 (first aborted on a
full disk mid docker-build, second started immediately):
- 12:09:15 spa_refresh wrote lib/apps/fabro-spa/assets/index.html
  (referencing entry-pw97apn6.js) AND removed_stale_entries emptied
  assets/assets/ — the plan came from a half-written dist
- 12:10:41 dist rebuilt (entry-34ptkwsq) by the other run
- result: embedded bundle = index.html WITHOUT any hashed assets;
  the follow-up image compiled the broken set and shipped a UI that
  404'd every asset while health + CLI stayed green (caught by the new
  just-smoke, commit 0d709ac64)

Two structural windows in spa_refresh.rs:
1. remove_stale_entries deletes before copies land: a crash (or a
   second run's mirror) between delete and copy leaves index.html
   present + assets gone — the worst combination, because index still
   references what is missing.
2. dist is a shared mutable directory: run_bun_build rebuilds it in
   place while another process (second just up, parallel cargo dev)
   may mirror it concurrently.

## Fix directions

- mirror into staging first, then ATOMIC swap (rename) of the whole
  assets dir — delete+copy never observable
- or: verify after refresh that every asset referenced by the embedded
  index.html exists in the embedded dir; refuse (exit 1) otherwise —
  'cargo dev build/docker-build' must not compile an inconsistent
  bundle (the new smoke then guards the deployed side)
- serialize: a lockfile under tmp/ for spa refresh + bun build

## Acceptance

- reproducer: run refresh against a dist being rewritten concurrently;
  embedded dir stays consistent (old or new, never mixed/empty)
- post-condition check wired into spa refresh + build
- just smoke stays green through a normal up
closeReason:
FIXED (commit ba8e5277c on denkhaus, deployed via just up, smoke 7/7 green incl. 'index references assets').

Both structural windows closed in spa_refresh.rs:
1. Ordered atomic publish (publish_staging): additive copies first, index.html flip LAST (only file referencing hashed assets by name), stale removal after the flip; every file replaced via temp+rename -> crash/full-disk at ANY point leaves old or new bundle, never a mix.
2. Index-reference verification: root-relative src=/href= targets must resolve; refuses a mixed staging snapshot BEFORE touching the embedded dir (deterministic reproducer test refresh_mixed_snapshot_refuses_before_touching_embedded_dir) and re-verifies post-publish so cargo dev build/docker-build never compiles an inconsistent bundle.
3. SpaRefreshLock (tmp/fabro-dev-spa.lock, pid, stale-break via /proc or 30min age) serializes bun build + mirror + publish across direct cargo dev invocations; just up keeps its pipeline flock; spa check takes the same lock.

Verified: 26/26 fabro-dev tests, clippy -D warnings green, fmt green, live E2E just up (bun build -> publish -> docker-build -> deploy -> smoke 7/7).

title: CLI: fabro ask prints the answer twice (deltas AND assistant_message both rendered)
description:
## Failure (reproduced 2026-08-25)

```console
$ fabro ask 01M0WW --prompt "Reply with exactly this token and nothing else: ECHO9T" --quiet
ECHO9TECHO9T
```

Every answer appears doubled on stdout — independent of --quiet/--json
(--json shows the same text twice as assistant_delta + assistant_message
events, which is correct THERE) and independent of tty/nohup. Confirmed
against the deployed 0.335.0-nightly.1 binary via two identical tokens.

## Root cause

lib/apps/fabro-cli/src/commands/run/ask.rs, render_event():

- "run.session.assistant_delta" branch: print!()s the delta (streaming)
- "run.session.assistant_message" branch: println!()s the FULL text again

Both render in text mode, so the answer prints once as the accumulated
deltas and once as the final message. Compare attach.rs, which gates its
final render on never having streamed deltas.

## Fix

Track whether any delta was rendered in text mode; skip the
assistant_message println when deltas already covered the content (or
print only a trailing newline then). Non-streaming sessions (no deltas
seen) keep the final println as the only output. --json path is fine as
is.

## Acceptance

- ask --quiet prints the answer exactly once
- session that streams deltas: text mode shows the stream, no duplicate
- session without deltas (if any): final message still prints
- regression test asserting byte-identical single output (two-token
  probe like the reproducer)

## Impact

scripts/run_workflow.nu currently works around this by parsing the JSONL
turn.succeeded event instead of stdout; a fix removes the workaround.

   'running now' from 'replaying 20 minutes ago'.

## Acceptance

- ps behavior for terminal runs decided and documented
- regression test: attach output of a finished run contains the marker,

title: PR publish uses run model glm-5.3 although [run.pull_request] model=glm-4.7 is configured (config never reaches resolve_pr_model)
description:
## Failure (run 01M0X36ZX6, 2026-08-25T18:35:11Z)

Server log at publish:

    WARN run{id=01M0X36ZX6}: fabro_workflow::pipeline::pull_request:
    PR content generation failed; using deterministic fallback title and
    skeleton body model=glm-5.3 error=LLM generation failed: No object
    generated: Failed to parse response as JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1

Configuration (think branch worlds, .fabro/project.toml, BOTH worlds):

    [run.pull_request]
    model = "zai:glm-4.7"   # non-reasoning, cheap, clean JSON for titling

The run model glm-5.3 fired, NOT the configured glm-4.7.

## Key evidence

- resolve_pr_model (operations/start.rs:713) has TWO early returns that
  fall back to the run model WITHOUT warning: pr_config=None and
  config.model=None. Only an UNRESOLVABLE ref warns
  ('could not be resolved to a concrete model').
- The deployed binary CONTAINS that warn string, but the server log for
  the affected runs shows NO such warn => the resolve path returned
  run_model via an early return: the PR config (or its model field) is
  None by the time the worker resolves it.
- Run was created host-side ('just run hello' -> fabro create) in the
  denkhaus-lab checkout whose project.toml carries the setting; the
  worker runs server-side on the persisted run spec — suspicion: the
  persisted PullRequestSettings lose the model field (serde drop,
  wrong layer read, or create/start not passing it).
- glm-5.3 failing the structured call reproduces fabro-c7f7's symptom
  class exactly (non-JSON output, no reasoning_effort on this call).

## Investigate

1. Trace [run.pull_request].model from host project.toml -> fabro
   create request -> persisted run spec -> worker resolve_pr_model:
   where does it become None?
2. Add an INFO log in resolve_pr_model on the success path stating the
   resolved PR model, and a WARN on the config.model=None early return
   when [run.pull_request] exists but carries no model (distinguishes
   'unset' from 'lost').
3. Re-check fabro-21c1 under this light: its premise ('glm-4.7 call
   fails') was never true — glm-4.7 never fired.

## Acceptance

- a lab run publishes with model=glm-4.7 in the log (no fallback)
- config plumbing has a test: persisted spec keeps pull_request.model
- the confusing case is observable: distinct log lines for unset vs
  unresolvable vs resolved PR model

## Related

- fabro-21c1 (open): same symptom, revised diagnosis needed
- fabro-c7f7 (closed): original structured-output failure on glm-5.3
closeReason: Root cause found: STALE SERVER BINARY, not config loss. Run 01M0X36 executed on 0.335.0-nightly.1 (events.jsonl version field) which pre-dated a1e27c9bf (2026-08-24, the dedicated-PR-model feature). That binary had no resolve_pr_model/pr_content_model at all — the PR content call always used the run model glm-5.3, whose non-JSON structured output triggered the fallback. The persistence suspicion is disproven: the spec blob of 01M0X36 contains pull_request.model=zai:glm-4.7 (fabro dump run.json). Fix = a1e27c9bf + deploy of 0.337.0-nightly.0 (2026-08-26, this session). Live proof run 01M0Z9WJGZ ('just run hello'): spec carries the model, no resolve warn, PR #7 published with GENERATED title 'Add haiku to README to demo basic Fabro workflow' and generated body, $0.03 total. Diagnostic lesson: for 'config never reaches X' bugs, check the executing binary's version in events.jsonl FIRST (fabro dump), before tracing serde/layering.

title: engine: materialize run warnings/errors into the worktree (.fabro/logs/) at run finalization
description:
User ask (2026-08-27, after run 01M11P68SHFS): errors and warnings that appear in the worker tracing log should be persisted under .fabro/ in the repository BY THE WORKFLOW, not via an external just command after the fact.

Today:
- Per-run tracing logs ARE persisted server-side (Storage::runtime_directory().logs_dir(); fabro logs <run-id> reads them — WARN lines like write_locks and PR-content fallback are all there).
- But they never reach the repo: the run branch/PR carries no record, and the improve review (which consumes events, not tracing) cannot see them. Events-vs-tracing separation stays per events-strategy.md — this is NOT a request for warning Event variants.

Design (journal precedent fabro-31b2 — the stage-journal bridge hands context_updates to hooks):
- At run finalization, the worker extracts WARN/ERROR lines from its own per-run tracing log (the file it already writes to logs_dir) and writes a digest .fabro/logs/<run-id>/warnings.md into the SANDBOX WORKTREE (header: run id, stage attribution where the span carries one, raw line otherwise).
- The final worktree commit then carries the digest onto the run branch -> PR -> base branch; the improve review and humans see it in-repo.
- Size-bounded (cap the digest; full log stays in server storage) and failure-never-breaks-the-run (side-effect only, like the journal hook).

Why not a run_complete hook: sandbox hooks cannot reach the server log store (d810: no fabro CLI/server access inside the product sandbox); host hooks write on the server host, not into the sandbox worktree — only the engine sits on both sides.

Open design question (user decision): should product-facing degradations (PR-content fallback used, Slack notification failed) ALSO become run events so fabro events/improve see them without file indirection? Events-strategy says events are product-facing state transitions — the PR-fallback arguably qualifies; discuss before implementing.

Done when a twin develop run's run branch contains .fabro/logs/<run-id>/warnings.md with the injected WARN lines, and a red-injected run shows its errors there too.
closeReason: Superseded by the Workflow-Revisor design (ADR-0011, grill 2026-08-27): live read-only tools replace materialized archives. Per-run tracing logs already persist server-side (fabro logs); the revisor reaches them via the new fabro_run_logs tool for Ask-Fabro analysts (follow-up seed). No engine materialization of logs/metrics into the worktree; no warning events (events-vs-tracing separation stays).

title: engine: fabro_run_logs — read-only tracing-log tool for Ask-Fabro analysts
description:
Prerequisite for the Workflow-Revisor (ADR-0011). Approved in the 2026-08-27 grilling.

Requirements:
- New read-only tool `fabro_run_logs { run_id, level?, tail? }` exposing one run's persisted worker tracing log (Storage runtime logs_dir, the same data `fabro logs` reads) to Ask-Fabro analyst sessions.
- Registered for Ask-Fabro by adding it to ASK_FABRO_RUN_TOOL_NAMES; scope rules identical to the other run tools (run-scoped backend rejects cross-run calls).
- WARN/ERROR lines are the primary consumer interest; default filter level WARN, redaction via the existing redaction pipeline before anything leaves the tool.
- Size-bounded response (tail window), full log stays in server storage.
- Twin tests: scoped access, redaction, level filter, cross-run rejection.

Done when an Ask-Fabro session (fabro ask) can answer 'which warnings did this run emit' from the tool alone.
closeReason:
DONE and LIVE-VERIFIED (2026-08-27, commit 48cc0217e, deployed via just up, smoke 7/7 green).

Live proof: fabro ask 01M11P68SHFS165HP9ATK6094V 'which warnings did this run emit' — the Ask-Fabro analyst called fabro_run_logs unprompted and answered precisely: 19 matching lines, no errors, two warning classes (write_locks 18x during implementer batches; PR content fallback 1x) — exactly matching the known server-log content.

Implementation: fabro-tool/src/logs.rs (severity filter with continuation-line inheritance, tail window 1..=1000 default 200, redaction via fabro_redact::redact_string); FabroToolBackend::get_run_logs with unavailable-default (pair precedent); ClientBackend through the existing run-scoped GET /runs/{id}/logs; registered in shared catalog + workflow dispatch + ASK_FABRO_RUN_TOOL_NAMES. Verification: fabro-tool 58 / fabro-workflow 1276 / fabro-server 870 tests, clippy + rustfmt clean.

Note: severity enum ordering and the ISO-timestamp check each had a bug caught by the module tests (not by review — the guide was loaded late in this cycle; process fix recorded in the iterate skill, phase 3 proof-of-work).

title: engine: fabro_ask + fabro_runs_list stage tools with inspects scope
description:
Prerequisite for the Workflow-Revisor (ADR-0011). Approved in the 2026-08-27 grilling.

Requirements:
- `fabro_ask { run_id, question }` for agent stages: engine creates an Ask-Fabro run session on the TARGET run id (create_run_session + submit turn, streaming to terminal) and returns the analyst's answer text to the stage. Reuses the Ask-Fabro system prompt and analyst toolset (events, get, run_logs).
- `fabro_runs_list { workflow?, since? }` read-only enumeration for bookkeeping (backed by the list-runs API; workflow filter on workflow_slug).
- Scope class: the revisor workflow's graph declares `inspects = "develop"` (node or graph attribute); the stage's worker token may create analyst sessions on and read exactly the runs of the declared workflows — nothing else. Server auth middleware gains this worker-token path (today create_run_session requires a user principal).
- Wiring: the dead `fabro_run_tools: Option<FabroRunToolServices>` producer finally exists — engine constructs the services for runs whose graph declares revises (ADR-0011 notes the bridge is fully built, only the producer is missing).
- Sentinel contract tests (distinct fixture values per options field at every boundary — the a1e27c9bf lesson): the model/tools arriving at the analyst session and the scope checks.

Done when a twin workflow stage can ask a question about another run and receives the analyst's answer, with cross-workflow targets rejected.

---

## Implementation design (2026-08-31, before code; ADR-0011 vocabulary)

Bridge status: the producer EXISTS since the fabro_run_logs cycle —
`run.agent.fabro_tools = true` -> worker token `agent:run_tools` scope ->
`build_fabro_run_tool_services` (cli runner.rs) -> `with_fabro_run_tools`.
Remaining work is exactly: inspects scope, two tools, server auth paths.

1. **Graph attribute (fabro-types):** graph-level `inspects = "develop"` /
   comma-separated slugs. `Graph::revises()` parses, trims, dedupes,
   drops empties. Node-level is intentionally NOT implemented v1: the
   worker token is issued per RUN, a node-level declaration would have to
   widen the run-wide token anyway; revisit only if per-node narrowing is
   ever needed.
2. **Worker token (fabro-server/worker_token.rs):** claims gain
   `inspects: Vec<String>` (skip when empty). `WorkerScopeSet` gains
   `inspects: Vec<String>`; issuance (`worker_launch_spec`) reads
   `run_state.spec.graph.revises()` and only attaches revises together
   with `agent:run_tools` (revises without run tools is meaningless).
3. **Server auth:**
   - create_run_session + submit turn(-stream): accept worker principal
     whose revises contains the TARGET run's `spec.workflow_slug`
     (handler-side check via run reader). User path unchanged.
   - list_runs: `ListRunsParams` gains `workflow`; store query gains
     `workflow_slug` (runs table has the column). A worker principal
     MUST filter and only to workflows in its revises (else 403);
     users unrestricted.
4. **fabro-tool:** `fabro_ask { run_id, question }` -> backend creates
     the session, submits the turn, consumes the SSE stream until
     terminal, returns the final `run.session.assistant_message` text
     (CLI ask.rs pattern). `fabro_runs_list { workflow?, since? }` ->
     list-runs API with workflow filter; `since` = created_at lower
     bound. Client-side: FabroRunToolServices carries `inspects`
     (runner decodes its own token claims); ask/list validate targets
     against it first, server re-checks (defense in depth).
5. **Registration gate:** `register_fabro_run_tools` registers
     fabro_ask/fabro_runs_list only when services.revises is non-empty;
     execution errors early on empty inspects. Ask-Fabro analyst sessions
     (ASK_FABRO_RUN_TOOL_NAMES) unchanged: events/get/logs only.
6. **Tests:** sentinel contract tests per field (a1e27c9bf lesson);
   twin workflow stage asks across runs and receives the analyst answer;
   cross-workflow target rejected (403 -> tool error); worker list-runs
   scope rejections; graph parsing; store workflow filter.

Note: fabro_ask blocks the stage until the analyst turn reaches a
terminal event (minutes possible). Accepted for v1; the revisor is the
only caller and its prompts are single-question.

---

## Post-review decisions (2026-08-31)

- Attribute renamed `revises` -> `inspects` (user decision; ADR-0011
  amendment): name the capability, not the revisor motive.
- Tool param is `created_since` (not `since`): agent-facing precision,
  matches the API query parameter 1:1.
- inspects_allows() encodes the `agent:run_tools` coupling in code, not
  just docs.
- Known scope gap (pre-existing, documented): the LEGACY run-tool routes
  (fabro_run_get/events on arbitrary runs) are NOT restricted by
  inspects; only ask/session + enumeration paths are. Follow-up: the
  legacy-scope hardening seed (fabro-4556).

---

## CLOSED 2026-08-31 (commit 5dd9ad8ca)

Delivered: graph attribute inspects, worker-token inspects claim
(coupled to agent:run_tools, byte-compatible legacy tokens), server

title: engine: surface write_locks concurrent-write warnings as counts, not repeated WARN lines
description:
Re-scoped (user directive 2026-08-27): the goal is NOT to aggregate or quiet the warning - the goal is to ELIMINATE ITS CAUSE.

Symptom: fabro_agent::write_locks logs 'concurrent write to the same file in one batch; serializing' 10+ times per run (run 01M11P68SHFS: implementer repeatedly writing main.go and fib_test.go). Benign in effect, but it means the engine receives MULTIPLE writes to the SAME file within one batch and must serialize them - a defect at the source, not a logging problem.

Investigate and fix the cause:
- WHERE do same-file parallel writes originate? Candidates: the agent batching several edit_file/apply_patch calls to the same path in one tool batch, parallel-branch handlers touching one file, or a retry duplicating a write.
- Fix at the layer that produces the batch: prevent same-file concurrent writes from being issued (coalesce them, reject the redundant ones with a clear error to the agent, or serialize at the tool-call boundary BEFORE the write-locks path).
- The write_locks warning then becomes unreachable for this class - keep it as a safety net for genuinely unexpected cases.

Done when a twin test reproduces a same-file multi-write batch and the fix prevents/deduplicates it at the source, and a live develop run produces ZERO write_locks warnings for this class.

title: engine: interview-question lifecycle notifications (push for HITL gates)
description:
Engine prerequisite for the workflow-revisor (ADR-0011) and the slack seed fabro-1ddb (lab tracker): slack lifecycle notifications currently fire ONLY on run.started / run.completed / run.failed (server.rs handle_lifecycle_event dispatch). A run parked at a human interview gate waits silently — unusable for cron-driven revisor runs that need an answer.

Requirements:
- New notifiable lifecycle event for a pending interview question (e.g. 'question.pending' in the events list of NotificationRouteSettings), carrying run id, run web url, question text (truncated), and timeout.
- Fires when a stage asks a question (QuestionAsked/interview-created path) and ideally re-fires nowhere else; question answered/cancelled/timeout stays run-internal.
- Route semantics follow the existing terminal-route model: enabled/provider/events/slack.channel per [run.notifications.*]; the revisor workflow (fabro-c74f) will configure its own route.
- Redaction: question text through the existing redaction pipeline.
- Twin tests: pending question dispatches exactly once to a configured route; run.completed/failed behavior unchanged; no notification when no route matches.

Done when a twin run with a question node and a configured route posts the question to the fake slack backend exactly once.

---

## Implementation design (2026-08-31, before code)

Findings: InterviewStarted already reaches the server's Slack service
(handle_event); today it ONLY feeds the default-channel interview bot
(with thread tracking + posted_messages state). The route-based
lifecycle dispatch (handle_lifecycle_event) never sees it.

Decisions:
1. ROUTE KEY = the real event name "interview.started" (not a new
   "question.pending" alias): NotificationRouteSettings.events is a
   plain Vec<String> matched against event_name(); using the true name
   adds zero vocabulary and zero mapping (naming lesson: no new
   public-contract name when the honest one exists). Alias can be
   added later if desired.
2. Dispatch: in handle_event's InterviewStarted arm, run the
   route-based lifecycle dispatch FIRST (after the empty-question_id
   guard), INDEPENDENT of the default-channel bot: no bot channel
   configured, bot already posted, or duplicate suppressions must not
   gate route notifications. The bot logic stays untouched.
3. Blocks: reuse slack_blocks::question_to_blocks (same visual
   language as the bot's questions; includes run id/url, options,
   buttons). Timeout: extend question_to_blocks with a timeout line
   when question.timeout_seconds is set — the bot path benefits too.
4. No prior-PR loading for questions (like run.started); workflow
   label resolution already falls back gracefully.
5. Redaction: inherited — events are redacted by build_redacted_event_
   payload in the event sink before the envelope reaches the service.
6. Tests (hermetic httpmock slack, existing rig): pending question
   posts exactly once to the configured route channel with question
   text + timeout + run url; no post when no route matches
   interview.started; run.completed behavior unchanged (existing
   tests); lifecycle question posts keep posted_messages empty (no bot
   state pollution).

---

## CLOSED 2026-08-31 (commit 789d76734)

Delivered per the design section: route key = 'interview.started'
(real event name), dispatch independent of the default-channel bot,

title: Graph-level retry policy with backoff config and node-level override for stage retries
description:
Stage retries today (lib/components/fabro-workflow/src/retry.rs) support node attributes 'retry_policy' (presets: none/standard/aggressive/linear/patient) and 'max_retries', plus a single graph attribute 'default_max_retries' that sets only the attempt count. The backoff shape is hardcoded (initial 5s, factor 2.0, cap 60s, jitter) and presets can only be selected per node.

Gap: transient provider errors (e.g. zai 429 rate limits) can hit ANY LLM node in a workflow, so the retry default belongs at workflow level. Today every LLM node repeats 'retry_policy=standard' manually (see revisor graph nodes select/analyze/file in run 01M1HKRE686W833SE86D8WD319); forgetting one node silently leaves it without retries.

Demand: declare a retry policy once at graph level (preset name, and optionally explicit backoff attributes initial_delay/factor/max_delay/jitter), applying to all nodes. Node attributes override the workflow default for special cases. Precedence: node retry_policy > node max_retries > graph retry_policy/backoff > graph default_max_retries > none. Exponential backoff with jitter already exists (fabro_util::backoff) and should stay the default shape.

title: Long-window rate limits defeat count-based retries: honor provider reset times or park-and-resume

Evidence: run 01M1HKRE686W833SE86D8WD319 burned its full stage retry budget (5 attempts, exponential backoff 5s..40s, ~2 min total) against a zai 429 whose usage window reset only hours later ('Usage limit reached for 5 hour. Your limit will reset at 2026-09-03 05:35:16'). The provider sent retry_after=null; the reset timestamp exists only inside the error message text. Three nested retry layers (agent.llm.retry x3, stage retries x5) all exhaust quickly against a multi-hour window, then the run soft-exits.

Count-based exponential backoff cannot bridge multi-hour provider windows: the delays are far too short and the attempt count exhausts within minutes while the limit stays.

Fix directions to evaluate: (1) parse provider reset/retry-after hints (header AND message text) and cap or extend retry delays accordingly; (2) a wall-clock retry budget option (retry until T) instead of/in addition to attempt counts; (3) park-and-resume semantics: on a long-window 429, park the run in a resumable state with a scheduled wake-up instead of exhausting retries and exiting. Related: fabro-18a5 (soft-exit runs cannot be resumed), fabro-83af (graph-level retry defaults).

title: rewind/fork UX: starting a fork with checkpoints ends terminal failed(terminated) — queue forks in resume mode or auto-switch
description:
Scope NARROWED 2026-09-03 after verification on merged v0.345.0-nightly.0 (merge 6530c724f): upstream PR #838 fixed the crash-loop half — see VERIFIED below. What remains is fix direction (1): the happy path. `fabro rewind`/`fabro fork` produce a fork that CARRIES checkpoint history, but `fabro start <fork>` queues Start mode, hits the checkpoint precondition, and the fork ends terminal failed(terminated) within seconds. The rewind output already prints the correct recovery hint ("To resume: fabro resume <fork-id>"), so the remaining work is UX: queue forks in Resume mode by default (or have start auto-detect checkpoint history and switch), so users do not have to know the mode rule. Fix direction (3) (respawn backoff) is obsolete — no respawn happens anymore.

Original report: after 'fabro rewind 01M1HKRE686W833SE86D8WD319 @41' (fork to 01M1JX979PTSZRZ10ZCTMJA34E), 'fabro start <new-run>' produced an infinite worker crash loop: every worker invocation died with 'Precondition failed: checkpoint already exists in the run store — did you mean to resume?' and the scheduler respawned it ~10x/second for minutes. Root cause: forked runs carry checkpoint history; queue_run_start (lib/apps/fabro-server/src/server/handler/lifecycle.rs) selects RunExecutionMode::Start for non-resume starts; operations::start refuses runs with existing checkpoints; the worker-exit failure event was rejected ('invalid status transition: runnable -> failed(terminated)') so the run stayed Runnable and spawn_scheduler retried forever. Correct recovery was 'fabro resume <fork-id>' (mode Resume), which worked.

VERIFIED 2026-09-03 on v0.345.0-nightly.0 (server built from merge 6530c724f): reproduced the exact scenario — unarchived 01M1HKRE686W833SE86D8WD319, `fabro rewind ... @41` -> fork 01M1MG3JYMZ8DJW0G09QXKEH0Z, `fabro start` -> ONE worker invocation, worker stderr shows the precondition failure, run persists as terminal failed(terminated) (~4s from start to terminal; server log shows a single worker control-stream, zero respawns; second start attempt correctly rejected 409 'status is failed(terminated), expected submitted'). Both test runs re-archived afterwards.

title: Designed loops exhaust per-node max_visits and fail as workflow_error 'stuck in a cycle'
description:
Evidence: revisor run 01M1JXPAABBQ3TM3DJ2DQ1VZDW (forked from 01M1HKRE686W833SE86D8WD319 at checkpoint @41) resumed cleanly, ran select@11 successfully (selected target 01M11P68SHFS165HP9ATK6094V), then terminated as failed/workflow_error: 'node "analyze" visited 10 times (node limit 10); run is stuck in a cycle'. The original run would have hit the same wall one stage later even without the zai 429 — the budget was already spent after 10 completed revision cycles.

Problems: (1) the revisor graph (digraph Revisor) is a designed loop with a natural end ('Nothing to revise' edge), but per-node max_visits (analyze=10, file=10, select=15) turns a healthy, still-productive loop into a hard workflow_error once the budget is gone and backlog remains — 'stuck in a cycle' is misleading for a loop that is making progress each visit; (2) node visit counts persist across fork/resume, so forking a long-running loop near its budget cannot continue it at all — the fork burns a cycle and dies; (3) there is no graceful 'budget exhausted, park and re-enter next pass' terminal state distinct from an error.

Fix directions: distinguish progress-making loops from true cycles (e.g. only fail as stuck-in-cycle when a node repeats without forward state change / same failure signature), or add a designed 'budget exhausted' exit kind (soft/boundary) so loops can park resumably, and/or revisit the revisor graph's per-node caps (graph max_node_visits=30 already bounds the run).

title: Per-node skills and memory scoping for agent stages
description:
Evidence: revisor run 01M1HKRE686W833SE86D8WD319 — every agent stage carries ~50 skill descriptions (~1.5k tokens) plus AGENTS.md memory (5.3KB) in its system prompt, regardless of need. Validation pass 01M1M568F5BZ9F17T3SFGRDCZ3 (2026-09-03) proved node attribute project_memory=false is INERT for agent nodes: AgentSession::initialize (lib/components/fabro-agent/src/session.rs ~line 625) calls discover_memory unconditionally; project_memory only gates the older prompt-handler path (lib/components/fabro-workflow/src/handler/prompt.rs line 68). select/analyze still loaded AGENTS.md (5307 bytes, budget 32768) with the attribute set.

Cover BOTH: (a) memory — honor project_memory=false (or a dedicated memory=false) in AgentSession::initialize/AgentConfig; (b) skills — a per-node attribute (skills=false or skills=<dir>) to disable or scope skill discovery (AgentSession config already has skill_dirs, node-level override is missing). title: Enforce journal keys in the routing output schema (painpoint mandate has no teeth)
description:
Evidence: develop prompts have mandated context_updates.journal with BOTH keys (painpoints, observations; empty valid, absence an error) since 2026-08-25 (fabro-e7c4) — yet the revisor run's journal analysis found exactly ONE painpoint entry across six develop-run journals (analyze@9: reviewers did the evidence-blob detour and logged zero). Demand: extend routing_validator (or add a graph/node opt-in like journal_required) to require context_updates.journal.painpoints (array) and .observations (array) when the node declares it; a missing journal triggers the existing output_retries re-ask. Empty arrays remain valid — the point is that silence stops passing as success. Apply to develop planner/implementer/reviewer and revisor select/analyze/file.

title: Degrade on unsupported model control instead of dead-ending
description:
Configure fallbacks in the run's model settings and/or add engine behavior to retry once with the unsupported control dropped on api_deterministic/invalid_request. Run 01M0QJ01P9E6EKX8S6TQN91G8E had max_attempts=5 but will_retry=false and fallbacks = {}, so one parameter mismatch consumed the whole goal-gated run even though the error message contained the remedy. Expected effect: model swaps or control drift degrade a single call to defaults instead of failing the run.

DESIGN INPUT 2026-09-03 (zai probe, api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4): control vocabularies differ per model - glm-4.7 rejected enable_thinking=false with code 1210 naming its real vocabulary (low, high, max), while thinking:{type:disabled} was silently accepted-but-weakened; glm-5.3 honors thinking:{type:disabled} fully. A future generic reasoning-off control should map per model family (thinking.type for glm-5.3-class, reasoning_effort=low where thinking cannot be disabled), and api_deterministic errors carrying the remedy vocabulary (like 1210) are exactly the retry-with-control-dropped trigger this seed asks for.

title: evidence: survive summary:high stage-renderer tail_lines cap (119 lines omitted hid the seed-work diff)
description:
Adopt from run 01M0NTS5XCXJ4V88M9MQWKD83G (analysis complete).

## Root cause (two truncation layers)

Layer 1 (OURS, working): evidence.nu self-budgets to 6.8k chars — the
output itself was complete and in-budget.

Layer 2 (ENGINE, the killer): summary:high's per-stage section renders
command output via tail_lines(...) — the reviewer's prompt received the
evidence section as '(119 lines omitted)' + tail, hiding the integrity
header and the ENTIRE main.go diff. Second cycle: 144 lines omitted,
identical rejection. The tool-less reviewer correctly refused to approve
invisible evidence twice; planner@3 correctly escalated Blocked (cycle
guard worked); seed fabro-8d26 remains open though code is verified.

## Fix (workflow side, within our control)

The evidence capture must fit the RENDERED budget, not the raw output
budget: tail_lines appears to keep ~the last N lines and drop the head —
exactly where our critical-first sections live.

1. Measure the effective rendered cap empirically (prompt #3 evidence
   section: ~119+visible lines -> derive chars).
2. Rearchitect evidence.nu: the reviewer's verdict-critical material is
   the DIFF — emit it FIRST inside command.output (tail_lines keeps the
   tail... so instead: emit ONLY a compact integrity header + diff
   tail-budgeted to the renderer's window, dropping our own nice-to-have
   sections) OR move review to a node that renders full output.
3. Engine-side (companion on denkhaus, update fabro-9467/fabro-e47c):
   per-node preamble scoping lets the reviewer see ONLY the evidence —
   no other stages, no renderer caps on the one input that matters.

## Acceptance

- a run whose seed-work diff is ~120 lines reaches the reviewer FULLY
  rendered (no 'omitted' inside the evidence section)
- reviewer approves a green-gate pass on visible evidence in one cycle
- fabro-8d26 (verified correct) closes on the next run

title: planner painpoint claims must be verified — deliver via context relay, not stated files

Planner@3's response claimed 'both painpoints are recorded in

## Fix (workflow side)

The prompt contract says 'append one JSON line to the staged file' —
the model claims the action without performing it (classic unverified
claim). Options:

1. planner.md: mandate an explicit verify step — after writing, `cat`
   the staged file and quote its line count in the response; the
   reviewer-side check: response claims must cite file line counts.
2. Stronger (engine, fabro-176b already filed): post-stage hook appends

3. Short-term deterministic: a tiny pre-refiner command node that
   extracts painpoints from context.workflow_painpoints into the staged
   file (context is engine-verified, unlike claimed file writes).

Option 3 removes the trust gap without engine changes: implement as
`stage-painpoints.nu` between planner and refiner? Evaluate during
implementation; option 1 is the 5-minute stopgap.

  caught (verify-step or deterministic relay)

## LINK (2026-08-23): message-bus seed fabro-meta-8652

The trust failure documented here (planner claiming unwritten painpoint
files) is failure class 1 of three relay failures; the message-bus
concept replaces the LLM relay entirely (message_send tool with
engine-added sender provenance).

title: develop: stale-base awareness after publish_blocked runs (unmerged run-branch remediation)
description:
## Context

fabro-67e5 landed on the platform (denkhaus 7d4176995): a green graph whose
publish failed now terminates as succeeded(publish_blocked) with a
PublishFailed failure detail and remediation text; Slack sees run.completed
(not run.failed). The workflow side (graph, prompts, notifications config)
needed no structural change — verified 2026-08-25 against meta/denkhaus-lab.

## Problem

With auto_merge enabled, a publish_blocked run means NO PR was created (or
push failed entirely), so the run branch fabro/run/<id> holds work that will
never merge back. The NEXT run clones the stale base:

- the planner may re-implement work that already sits on an unmerged run
  branch (its verification-only path only fires when acceptance criteria
  happen to look satisfied in the stale worktree)
- nothing in the loop (prepare, evidence, closeout) surfaces that the base
  is behind unmerged run branches
- the Slack remediation is the only signal; nobody acts on it autonomously

## Candidate directions (decide together)

1. prepare step: detect unmerged fabro/run/* branches ahead of base and
   fail fast / annotate context (cheap git, deterministic)
2. closeout: when tracker_empty routes to exit, check for unmerged run
   branches and surface them in the terminal context
3. evidence: include 'branches ahead of base' in the capture so the
   reviewer/planner can see them
4. accept as-is: Slack is the human signal; document the manual remediation
   (open PR from fabro/run/<id>) as the run branch being the durability path

## Acceptance

- decision recorded (ADR or seed note) on which direction(s) ship
- if 1-3 ship: deterministic, no LLM, tested against a run branch ahead
  of base
